record.title: Source-aligned agent-memory units improve complete-evidence retrieval in a synthetic trace benchmark
record.summary: A paper introduces Execution Provenance Graph Memory (EPGM) for retrieving complete supporting evidence from long agent execution histories under a fixed token budget. On 2,000 queries over 1,207 held-out ISETrace trajectories, the authors report that source-aligned provenance units improve Full Support@2048 by 19.07 points over flat 512-token windows and by 11.96 points over a per-metric oracle across four flat chunk sizes, with matched Dense-FT scoring. Holding candidate units and seed scores fixed, a graph-conditioned residual adds a smaller 4.55 points (95% CI 2.98–6.18), concentrated on queries whose evidence spans multiple events. The corpus is synthetic and the results are author-reported; no independent reproduction was performed.
organizations: Southern University of Science and Technology

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The authors define an execution-provenance retrieval method and evaluate it on ISETrace, a synthetic corpus of agent/tool trajectories; the paper reports a human audit of 500 test queries.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On 2,000 test queries over 1,207 held-out trajectories, matched Dense-FT scoring with source-aligned provenance units improves Full Support@2048 by 19.07 points over flat 512-token windows and 11.96 points over a per-metric oracle across four flat chunk sizes.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: With candidate units and seed scores fixed, the graph-conditioned residual adds 4.55 Full Support@2048 points (95% CI [2.98, 6.18]); the paper reports that the benefit is concentrated when evidence spans multiple events.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The authors state that ISETrace is synthetic and that exact trajectory disjointness does not ensure zero overlap in normalized intent text; they do not claim that observable graph links establish causal dependency.

evidence_gaps.description: The reported candidate-view and graph-residual gains have not been independently reproduced.
The benchmark uses synthetic trajectories; performance on naturally occurring agent histories and real downstream tasks is unknown.

brief.importance_rationale: If independently reproduced on real agent histories, complete-evidence retrieval under a fixed token budget could materially improve long-context agent reliability; the controlled separation of source-aligned candidate gains from graph gains may guide memory-system choices. Score 5 reflects the potential research and engineering consequence, not confidence in synthetic-benchmark transfer.
limitations: All quantitative findings are reported by the paper authors; this activation did not run the linked code or independently reproduce the benchmark.
ISETrace is a synthetic execution-grounded corpus, so the measured effects may not transfer to real, diverse agent histories, tools or memory queries.
Queries are model-authored and only a stratified subset of 500 receives human validation; the audit does not establish error-free labels for the full test set.
Trajectory-disjoint splits control exact trajectory overlap but do not guarantee zero overlap in normalized intent text.
The observed provenance graph records execution structure and lexical reuse; it does not establish semantic or causal dependency between events.
The reported full-support metric evaluates retrieval of annotated spans, not reliable downstream task completion or answer correctness outside a limited transfer analysis.

brief.summary: A paper introduces Execution Provenance Graph Memory (EPGM) for retrieving complete supporting evidence from long agent execution histories under a fixed token budget. On 2,000 queries over 1,207 held-out ISETrace trajectories, the authors report that source-aligned provenance units improve Full Support@2048 by 19.07 points over flat 512-token windows and by 11.96 points over a per-metric oracle across four flat chunk sizes, with matched Dense-FT scoring. Holding candidate units and seed scores fixed, a graph-conditioned residual adds a smaller 4.55 points (95% CI 2.98–6.18), concentrated on queries whose evidence spans multiple events. technical.claimed_result: For 2,000 span-grounded test queries over 1,207 held-out trajectories, source-aligned units improve Full Support@2048 by 19.07 points over flat 512-token windows and 11.96 points over a per-metric oracle across four flat chunk sizes. A graph-conditioned residual adds 4.55 points (95% CI [2.98, 6.18]) with candidates and seed scores fixed, mainly when evidence spans multiple events.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper and its reported protocol, comparisons, and limitations are publicly inspectable. The quantitative retrieval gains are author-reported and were not independently reproduced.
technical.implementation_status: Authors report a trained retrieval system and provide code and dataset links in the paper; neither artifact was executed or independently inspected in this activation.
technical.mechanism: The method aligns tool arguments and outputs to source-backed provenance units, scores candidates with dense retrieval, and optionally refines scores using a zero-initialized residual relational graph convolutional network over typed execution edges. Evaluation separates the candidate-view effect from the graph-conditioned residual by first matching Dense-FT scorers and then holding candidates and seed scores fixed.
technical.novelty: The benchmark measures whether all required source spans fit within a hard retrieval-token budget and uses shared source coordinates to distinguish source-aligned candidate construction from graph-based reranking gains.
technical.regime: Synthetic ISETrace corpus; 2,000 test queries over 1,207 trajectory-disjoint test trajectories, with a stratified human-audited subset of 500 queries. Primary metric is complete gold-span support within 2,048 tokens. Evidence consists of executed tool arguments and outputs; transfer to real-world agent histories is unknown.
technical.reproducibility: The paper specifies splits, seeds, paired comparisons and bootstrap intervals and links code/data. Results remain unreplicated here; the authors note synthetic traces and that trajectory separation does not eliminate overlap in normalized intent text.
technical.strongest_baseline: Matched Dense-FT scoring on flat 512-token windows, plus an oracle selecting the best of four flat chunk sizes per metric; for graph contribution, exact seed-score passthrough with the same provenance-unit candidates. These comparisons separate candidate construction from the learned graph residual.

brief.title: Source-aligned agent-memory units improve complete-evidence retrieval in a synthetic trace benchmark
brief.why_it_matters: If the reported result generalizes, representing tool arguments and outputs as source-aligned units may help agent memory return complete evidence within a context budget, while the matched controls suggest most measured improvement comes from candidate construction and a narrower portion from graph propagation. This could change memory-system evaluation and design, but the experiment uses synthetic execution traces and does not establish reliable downstream performance on real agents.
